key_insight: The paper explores whether on-policy self-distillation can work without privileged answers or extra visual evidence, relying only on input conditioning to create the learning signal. This points to a simpler form of self-distillation that removes the need for asymmetric side information.
problem_solved: It addresses the challenge of how to make self-distillation effective when the teacher and student do not have access to special extra information. The goal is to eliminate external teachers and other asymmetry sources while still keeping the self-teacher stronger than the student.
method: Start from on-policy self-distillation, where the model teaches itself from its own predictions.
Remove reliance on privileged answers and visual evidence as sources of teacher-student asymmetry.
Use input conditioning alone to create a stronger self-teacher signal for learning.
impact: This matters because it simplifies self-distillation pipelines and reduces dependence on extra annotations or specialized input setups. For practitioners, that can mean easier-to-deploy training methods with fewer assumptions and lower data engineering overhead.
